Diageo India (United 
Spirits Limited) is among India’s leading beverage alcohol (alcobev) companies with a portfolio of premium brands. A subsidiary of Diageo plc., it is listed in India on both the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) as United Spirits Limited (USL). Headquartered in Bengaluru, the Company manufactures, sells and distributes an outstanding collection of iconic Global and Indian brands, blending global expertise with local innovation to deliver world-class products and experiences to consumers.As USL leads and shapes 
the future of the alcobev industry in India, we remain equally committed to building a more sustainable, progressive, and inclusive world. Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) focus is at the heart of our business strategy, as outlined in our ‘Spirit of Progress’ agenda. This agenda is focused on pioneering grain-to-glass sustainability, championing inclusion and diversity, and promoting positive drinking all underpinned by doing business the right way.Contents

About the Report
This is the second Integrated Annual Report of United Spirits Limited (USL), also referred to as Diageo 
India or the Company. This Report presents a balanced view of our financial and non-financial performance, while explaining how we conduct our business, create value and deliver outcomes for our stakeholders, not limited to statutory requirements. It also provides insights into our business model, material matters, risks and opportunities, strategic priorities, governance practices, performance and outlook. Through these integrated disclosures, we aim to provide providers of financial capital and other stakeholders with relevant information to support informed decision-making.
Reporting Period  
and Scope
All financial and non-financial information presented in this 
Report pertains to USL, unless otherwise stated, for the period from April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026. Wherever relevant, we have included historical trends for key performance indicators, including ESG metrics, to help readers understand our value-creation journey more comprehensively.Reporting Framework, 
Guidelines and Standards
The Report should be read together with the annual accounts for a 
complete understanding of our financial performance.
• The narrative section of the Report follows the principles of the International Integrated Reporting Council’s Framework, overseen by the IFRS Foundation. 
• The statutory sections of the Report comply with, report on or reference applicable requirements and frameworks. These sections include:
 »Board’s Report
 »Management Discussion and Analysis
 »Corporate Governance Report
 »Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting
 »Financial Statements
• The applicable requirements and frameworks include:
 »Companies Act, 2013 and its associated rules
 »Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
 »Revised Secretarial Standards issued by The Institute of Company Secretaries of India
 »Indian Accounting Standards
 »National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct
 »United Nations Sustainable Development GoalsOur Capitals
Financial Capital
Financial capital represents the funds we generate 
and raise, which are prudently deployed across the business to create long-term value and deliver sustainable stakeholder returns.
Human Capital
Human capital reflects the passion, talent and consumer-first mindset of our people. We invest in their development and foster an equitable, inclusive and safe workplace that encourages creativity, innovation and independent thinking.
Social and Relationship Capital
Social and relationship capital represents the trust and enduring relationships we have built with stakeholders. Continuous engagement, responsiveness and long-term partnerships support our reputation, business strategy and licence to operate.
Natural Capital
Natural capital represents the resources essential to our operations, including water, energy and agricultural inputs, along with the environmental impact of our activities. Through ‘Grain to Glass Sustainability’, we continue to advance responsible and sustainable operations.Brand Capital
Brand capital reflects Diageo India’s reputation, consumer trust and emotional connection in the market. Our innovative, premium portfolio and impactful brand-building initiatives continue to strengthen brand perception and market position.
Manufactured Capital
Manufactured capital represents our manufacturing facilities, equipment and logistics infrastructure. Continued investments, global best practices and advanced technologies enable us to produce and deliver high-quality spirits efficiently, safely and sustainably.
Intellectual Capital
Intellectual capital comprises our expertise in processes, technologies and the craft of spirit-making. It drives innovation, strengthens our manufacturing, logistics and sales capabilities, and supports our digital transformation into a future-ready organisation.
Materiality 
Determination
Our double materiality assessment helps us identify the 
sustainability topics that matter most to our business and stakeholders. It looks at how these topics affect people, the environment and society, as well as how they can influence our financial performance. The findings support better decisions, stronger risk management, meaningful stakeholder engagement and long-term value creation. They also help us keep our priorities relevant in a changing business environment.Assurance
The financial statements presented in this Report have been audited by Price Waterhouse & Co Chartered Accountants LLP.
Reasonable assurance on the BRSR Core indicators has been 
provided by Price Waterhouse & Co Chartered Accountants  LLP. The scope and basis of assurance are detailed in the assurance report issued by Price Waterhouse & Co Chartered Accountants LLP.
All other financial and non-financial performance information  
has been internally verified and assured by the Management of the Company.

Chairperson’s 
Message
Against this backdrop, India continued to 
distinguish itself as one of the world's most resilient and attractive growth markets. Strong domestic demand, a young and aspirational consumer base, improving infrastructure, and growing strategic relevance in global trade have reinforced confidence in the country's long-term prospects.
It is within this context that United Spirits 
Limited (Diageo India) delivered another year of impressive performance and strategic progress. This was my first full year as Chairperson of the Company, and it has reinforced my conviction that we are exceptionally well positioned to benefit from the opportunities that lie ahead. FY 2025-26 was also the first full year under Praveen Someshwar's leadership as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer. The continuity of strategic direction that he has brought, combined with fresh energy, a clear consumer-first mindset, and disciplined execution, gives the Board considerable confidence as we enter the next phase of growth.Long-term value creation requires not only building exceptional assets but also allocating capital where it can generate the greatest strategic and financial returns. The Board believes this decision serves the long-term interests of all stakeholders.
Navigating a Changing 
Environment
The Board remains clear-eyed about both 
the challenges and opportunities that lie ahead.
Tensions in West Asia have disrupted 
shipping routes and contributed to higher logistic and packaging material costs during the latter part of the year. Volatility in crude oil prices created additional pressure on packaging inputs, while shifting trade policies and currency movements introduced uncertainty across global markets.
While these factors represent near-term 
headwinds, they also reinforce the importance of resilience, agility, and disciplined execution. The Board is encouraged by the actions management is taking to mitigate these pressures through productivity initiatives, supply chain optimisation, and constructive engagement with state authorities.
At the same time, periods of global 
disruption often reinforce structural advantages. India's growing importance as both a manufacturing hub and consumption market, its expanding network of trade relationships, and the resilience of its domestic demand story have become increasingly evident in the current environment.
In this context, the signing of the India-UK 
Free Trade Agreement is a development the Board views with considerable optimism. For India, the world's largest whisky market, the agreement has the potential to be transformative. Reduced tariffs on Scotch whisky will improve accessibility for consumers, support premiumisation within the category, and generate meaningful long-term cost benefits through lower import duties on bulk Scotch.Building a Future-Ready 
Organisation
Sustaining growth over the coming 
decade will require more than a strong portfolio. It will require an organisation that can adapt quickly, harness technology effectively, and attract and develop exceptional talent.
The Board is encouraged by the progress 
management has made in embedding AI and advanced analytics across the business. These capabilities are enhancing decision-making, improving agility, and creating meaningful operational advantages across commercial and supply chain functions.
Equally important is the Company's 
culture. Strong employee engagement scores and external recognition for inclusion and workplace excellence reflect an organisation that understands that long-term performance is built on people. The Board views talent, leadership, and culture as critical enablers of sustainable growth and enduring competitive advantage.
Investments in capability building are the 
pillars of the Company's next phase of growth. They will play an important role in ensuring that Diageo India remains well positioned to succeed in an increasingly dynamic marketplace.
Governance and Long term 
Stewardship 
The Board's responsibility extends 
beyond overseeing performance. It is to ensure that the Company is positioned to create value over the long term, while maintaining the trust of consumers, employees, communities, regulators, and shareholders. Throughout the year, the Board remained focused on effective governance, responsible marketing and consumption, robust risk management, and the development of a culture that reflects our values. We believe that companies that earn trust consistently are ultimately better positioned to sustain growth, navigate change, and create lasting value.Looking Ahead
What I find most encouraging, as I reflect on the year, is the extent to which the Company's relationship with India continues to deepen – through the communities it serves, the talent it nurtures, the brands it builds, and the long-term investments it makes. This connection is not simply a consequence of our strategy; it is central to it.
Our confidence in the future rests not 
only on the strength of our brands or the quality of our execution, but also on our conviction that India's growth story remains one of the most compelling in the world. The next chapter will reward businesses that combine ambition with discipline, growth with responsibility, and scale with trust.
United Spirits Limited is well positioned to 
be one of those businesses.
On behalf of the Board, I extend my 
sincere gratitude to Diageo plc, our employees, customers, partners, and to you, our shareholders, for your continued trust, commitment, and support.
Warm Regards
V K Viswanathan ChairpersonFY 2025-26 was a year in which 
the global operating environment became increasingly complex. Geopolitical tensions, evolving trade relationships, supply chain disruptions, currency volatility, and shifting patterns of global investment tested businesses across markets. Y et periods of uncertainty often reveal underlying strengths: of economies, institutions, and companies.
Transformational Years in the 
Making
Before reflecting on FY 2025-26, it is worth 
considering the journey that has brought us here. The transformation of Diageo India over the past five years has been significant by any measure.
The Company has delivered consistent 
growth, particularly in the Prestige & Above segment, expanded margins, strengthened its balance sheet, became debt-free, and built a surplus cash position that enabled a return to dividend distribution. At the same time, the portfolio has been reshaped through the divestment of non-core brands, increased investment behind premium and luxury offerings, the creation of new categories, and strategic investments in new growth engines.
More important than the financial 
outcomes, however, is what they represent. Through a series of strategic decisions made consistently over time, the Company has evolved into a business defined by sharper focus, stronger execution capabilities, and a commitment to superior long-term value creation. Performance and Capital 
Allocation
FY 2025-26 was led by continued 
momentum in the Prestige & Above segment. The Company delivered a healthy financial performance while continuing to invest behind its brands, capabilities, and growth agenda.
Reflecting the strength of this performance 
and the confidence in the Company's future prospects, the Board has recommended a final dividend of ` 11 per 
share, subject to shareholder approval. Together with the interim dividend the total for FY 2025-26 comes up to ` 17 per share, as compared to ` 12 per share in the previous year FY 2024-25. 
The year also saw a landmark strategic 
decision: the sale of the Company's 100% stake in Royal Challengers Sports Private Limited for approx. ` 16,663 Crores, representing a very attractive valuation. Its sale reflects a strategic choice to sharpen focus on building a leading premium beverage alcohol business and creating new categories and segments. It also demonstrates a disciplined approach to capital allocation. Dear Shareholders,

=== page 9 ===
For the alcobev industry, this shift carries 
particular significance. India is already the world’s largest whisky market and is increasingly emerging as a source of innovation and premium brands recognised well beyond its borders. What excites us even more is the structural shift underway within it — consumers today are not simply drinking more premium brands — they are engaging with brands differently. They are seeking authenticity, provenance, elevated experiences, and brands that reflect personal identity and aspiration. We believe we are uniquely positioned to lead in this environment.
Our confidence is grounded not only in 
the strength of the market opportunity, but in the capabilities we have built over time — a portfolio spanning multiple consumer occasions, deep distribution reach, strong execution capabilities, and an increasingly premium and innovation-led brand mix.
We continued to strengthen our route-to-
market capabilities, expand our premium portfolio, enhance supply chain resilience, and accelerate digital and data-led interventions across the business. At the heart of this progress is our talented team, whose passion, resilience, and commitment continue to define our culture and performance.environment, consumer profile, and pace 
of development. Our job is to navigate that complexity with agility, stay focused on our circle of control, and ensure that the tailwinds we cultivate consistently outpace the challenges we face.
Maharashtra presented our most 
significant near-term challenge. Significant excise duty increases resulted in sharp consumer price spikes, and the introduction of Maharashtra Made Liquor created additional competitive complexity at the lower end of the portfolio. We responded with discipline, restructuring our value chain in close alignment with our channel partners and reinforcing execution at the ground level. What this period reaffirmed above all is the structural strength of our brands.
At the same time, India was delivering 
meaningful tailwinds. Andhra Pradesh continued to grow strongly. Uttar Pradesh effectively doubled its licensed retail outlets through progressive policy reform. Karnataka introduced one of the most significant excise policy frameworks in years. Jharkhand, Rajasthan, and Madhya Pradesh all continued to progress. The structural drivers shaping India's consumption story are intact, and the anticipated India-UK Free Trade Agreement, adds a further meaningful tailwind.
Strengthening Our Portfolio
India is not one consumer market. It is three. A vast aspirational base seeking affordable access to better quality. A growing middle class premiumising with confidence. And an affluent segment demanding luxury experiences and repertoire variety. Our portfolio is built to serve all three, across BII and BIO whisky, white spirits, and Indian single malts, with differentiated strategies for each.
For our India 1 consumer, Royal 
Challenge grew ahead of the category, with the 180ml pocket pack delivering double-digit growth and expanding nationally. After a year of comprehensive work, we have also launched the most significant renovation of McDowell's No. 1 in its history: a re-engineered liquid with 30% more Scotch for a smoother, richer taste, a completely new pack design, and a new aspirational 180ml PET format, all at the same price point. Tested across eight markets with over 10,000 consumers, this transformed bundle has launched in Uttar Pradesh and will roll out pan-India through FY 2026-27.
For our India 2 consumer, Signature 
crossed the ` 1,000 Crores NSV milestone, building strong equity through purpose-led storytelling. Black and White emerged as the largest Scotch brand in India by volume, making India the number one market for this brand within Diageo globally. Black Dog gained strong traction through its Savour the Pause renovation featuring a campaign with Emilia Clarke.
At the top of the pyramid, Johnnie 
Walker strengthened its luxury credentials through the Icon Meets Icon campaign featuring Virat Kohli, title sponsorship of AP Dhillon's national tour, and the scale-up of Black Label Whisky Experiments into third-space environments. India is now the third-largest Johnnie Walker market globally by volume. Godawan earned over 100 awards in under two years, the fastest any single malt has reached this milestone globally and grew at triple digits through the year. The launch of Godawan 173 at The Savoy London during London Fashion Week, inspired by the recovery of the critically endangered Great Indian Bustard, reinforced our ambition to build Indian luxury brands that combine craftsmanship, conservation, and global cultural relevance.
Beyond whisky, Don Julio crossed ` 100 
Crores in NSV within nine months, our fastest brand to reach this milestone, capturing one-third of the Indian tequila market. Smirnoff crossed 1 million cases, propelling India into the top five Smirnoff markets globally, with a clear trajectory to ` 1,000 Crores in NSV over the next 18 months.
Building for What Comes Next
At the same time, we continued to invest behind future growth opportunities. The acquisition of NAO Spirits brought the pioneering craft brands Greater Than, Hapusa, and PIPA into the Diageo India portfolio, validating our belief in the long-term potential of locally rooted craft brands. Our increased stake in Sober (V9 Beverages) reflects our commitment to serving consumers across the full spectrum of how they choose to drink, including the growing trend toward moderation. The Good Craft Co. brings this ecosystem 
together, creating a platform where creators, consumers, and communities connect around innovation and craftsmanship in spirits.
Doing Business the right way
Equally important is our commitment to doing business responsibly. During the year, we continued to advance our sustainability agenda through water stewardship initiatives under The Godavari Initiative, renewable energy adoption, inclusion and diversity programmes, and skilling initiatives through Learning for Life. We remain clear that long-term growth must be both inclusive and sustainable as we continue to drive value for a Viksit Bharat. Our contribution has been significant. An independent Pahlé India Foundation study highlights that Diageo India contributed over ` 20,000 Crores 
in taxes and levies and created 6.5 Lakh Jobs for India’s Economy (direct + indirect) in F24 alone, making it one of the largest contributors to state revenues within the consumer sector. 
As I reflect on the year, what gives me the 
greatest confidence is the strength of the foundations we are building — stronger brands, sharper execution, disciplined capital allocation, and a talented organisation aligned behind a common ambition. This coupled with progressive policy developments across several states are also creating new opportunities for responsible and sustainable category growth. 
India’s next phase of growth will create 
enduring opportunities for businesses that combine scale with agility, ambition with discipline, and growth with responsibility. India has the potential to become one of the most important premium alcobev markets globally over the coming decade, and we intend to help shape that evolution.
I would like to thank my incredible team 
at Diageo India, customers, partners, shareholders, and Diageo plc for their continued trust and support.
Warm Regards
Praveen Someshwar Managing Director & CEOManaging Director 
& CEO's  Message
India is entering a new phase in 
its relationship with the world. Its growing economic influence, expanding trade relationships, and rising cultural confidence are reshaping global business priorities and how India sees itself. 
During the year, Diageo plc also entered 
an exciting new phase of leadership globally. Under the leadership of our Global CEO, Sir Dave Lewis, there is renewed focus on accelerating sustainable growth, strengthening consumer-centric innovation, and building future-ready brands and capabilities. This direction is strongly aligned with the opportunities we see in India.
Delivering with Discipline
FY 2025-26 was a year of disciplined execution and resilient growth, delivered against a backdrop of regulatory complexity and an uneven demand environment.
The Prestige and Above segment 
remained the cornerstone of our growth strategy, delivering healthy growth and contributing strongly to overall revenues. Gross margins expanded meaningfully through the year, driven by portfolio mix improvement, disciplined revenue growth management, and a largely benign commodity environment.
For the full fiscal year FY 2025-26, 
consolidated net sales reached ` 12,467 Crores, reflecting 7.7% growth, while standalone net sales grew 7.6% to ` 12,448 Crores. The Prestige and Above segment grew by 8.6%, contributing ` 11,152 Crores in net sales. Consolidated EBITDA grew by 11%, while standalone EBITDA rose 11.6% to ` 2,296 Crores. Consolidated PAT stood at ` 1,709 Crores and a net profit margin of 13.7%. Standalone PAT at ` 1,830 Crores with a margin of 14.7%, expanding by 123 bps year-on-year. The Board has recommended a final dividend of ` 11 per 
share, subject to shareholder approval.
A Strategic Milestone
In March 2026, we announced the sale of our 100% stake in Royal Challengers Sports Private Limited, which owns and operates the Royal Challengers Bengaluru IPL and WPL franchises, for a total consideration of ` 16,663 Crores. This is the highest valuation ever paid for a cricket franchise globally, a testament to the extraordinary asset built and stewarded over nearly two decades. Also noteworthy is that RCB departs as the reigning IPL and WPL champion. This transaction sharpens our focus squarely on our core beverage alcohol business and its considerable long-term potential, and the proceeds will support value creation for our shareholders.

VOur approach to stakeholder engagement is primarily 
guided by the Double Materiality Assessment process. This ensures focus on the issues that are most relevant and impactful. We maintain continuous dialogue and feedback with stakeholders to prioritise areas such as environmental stewardship, social equity, governance, product innovation and financial performance, aligning our strategy with evolving stakeholder expectations.We believe in governance that safeguards the interests of the Company while creating value for both shareholders and stakeholders. A cross-functional Diageo India Leadership Team, comprising functional heads, channels stakeholder perspectives to the Executive Committee, led by the Managing Director and CEO. The Executive Committee, in consultation with the Board, takes the necessary decisions to address stakeholder interests.
Our Approach to Stakeholder Engagement
Our Engagement Process
Mapping internal and external stakeholders to

We operate in an increasingly dynamic environment, and our integrated 
risk management framework enables timely identification, assessment, and mitigation of risks across the organisation. The framework supports informed and agile decision-making and is seamlessly integrated across strategic and operational activities. The Board through its committees provides rigorous oversight, ensuring strong governance, disciplined management of key risk areas, and timely action on emerging issues. This disciplined approach reinforces organisational resilience and supports the creation of sustained long-term value.Risk Management 
Behind GrowthResilience A structured, enterprise-wide 
risk management framework enables consistent identification, assessment, mitigation, and monitoring of risks across the organisation. Risk Management Process
Three-fold Risk Management CommitteeRisk ownership rests with functional teams as 
the first line of defence, supported by oversight from the Executive Committee through quarterly reviews as the second line. The Board Risk Management Committee conducts periodic assessments of key risks and the effectiveness of mitigation measures. Risks and mitigation actions are clearly defined, time-bound, and reviewed through established governance mechanisms, strengthening organisational resilience.

Management CommitteeProvides oversight of significant risk exposures and reviews

Drives the risk management process through structured 
discussions that integrate strategic direction (top-down) with operational insights (bottom-up).
Facilitates the identification and evaluation of risks through 
a bottom-up approach, incorporating relevant internal and external factors to support comprehensive risk assessment.
The Risk Management Committee identifies key risks as those with the most significant potential impact on the entity, including risks material to performance or those that could affect the business model, solvency, or liquidity. Additional risks, whether currently assessed as less significant or not yet identified, may also adversely impact the business. The following risks represent areas of continued focus across the alcobev industry including the Company amidst a dynamic business environment. Our material priorities reflect critical issues which shape our ability to grow 
responsibly in a regulated, resource-intensive industry. These priorities are aligned with our Spirit of Progress agenda. They guide how we manage risks, create value for our stakeholders, and ensure resilient, future-ready operations.Double Materiality Assessment
Shared PurposeEngaging for Approach to Double Materiality Assessment
From Dialogue to Direction
01
02
03
04
05United Spirits Limited’s FY 2025–26 Double Materiality 
Assessment marks a significant step forward in strengthening the integration of sustainability, risk management and long-term value creation within the Company’s strategic priorities. Building on the FY 2024–25 materiality framework, the assessment transitions from a primarily impact-led approach to a double materiality lens, considering both the Company’s impacts on society and the environment, as well as the financial implications of sustainability-related risks and opportunities on the business.
The assessment is aligned with Diageo PLC’s global ESG issues 
assessment and the Group’s ‘Spirit of Progress’ framework, while being contextualised to reflect India’s operating environment. This ensures continuity with Diageo’s global materiality universe and governance processes, while enabling United Spirits Limited to incorporate India-specific stakeholder perspectives, regulatory dynamics, community expectations and business realities.Through this approach, global ESG priorities have been translated into locally relevant material topics for Diageo India. The assessment places sharper emphasis on issues that are particularly salient in the Indian context, including water stewardship, sanitation and hygiene, prevention of harmful alcohol use, agri-food chain resilience, livelihoods and working conditions, waste reduction, inclusive growth, product safety and responsible corporate governance. These priorities reflect the Company’s exposure to local water stress, dependence on climate-sensitive agricultural value chains, a highly regulated alcobev sector, and the evolving expectations of consumers, communities, employees, investors and regulators.
Overall, the FY 2025–26 Double Materiality Assessment 
reflects the maturation of United Spirits Limited’s materiality approach. It reinforces alignment with Diageo PLC’s global ESG priorities while providing a more nuanced understanding of the sustainability topics most relevant to India. By integrating impact and financial perspectives, the assessment supports more informed decision-making, strengthens accountability and enhances the Company’s ability to create sustainable, responsible and resilient long-term value.

opportunities, anchored in Diageo plc's materiality universe and tailored to Diageo's Indian operating context.

Relevance to United Spirits Limited
Water is fundamental to the Company’s operations and value chain — from grain cultivation to distillation, bottling, cleaning, and the final consumer experience. With many manufacturing sites located in water-stressed regions of India, water availability and quality present both operational risks and a responsibility toward local communities. Securing long-term access to quality water, minimising withdrawal intensity and replenishing water in stressed catchments are central to business continuity and the Company's 'Grain-to-Glass' sustainability commitment.

Relevance to United Spirits Limited
As one of India's leading alcobev companies, the Company has both a direct responsibility and an opportunity to shape responsible 
drinking behaviours at scale. The 'Positive Drinking' agenda is highly relevant to the Company's long-term business sustainability, as it directly supports moderation, underage drinking prevention, drink-driving awareness and informed consumer choice. 
In a category subject to heightened social and regulatory scrutiny, proactive leadership on responsible consumption strengthens consumer trust, protects brand equity and reinforces USL’s licence to operate. By embedding Positive Drinking across brands, partnerships and stakeholder engagement, USL demonstrates industry leadership while contributing meaningfully to safer, more responsible drinking norms in India.
.Relevance to United Spirits Limited
Climate change is material to USL’s long-term resilience such as water stress, extreme weather and agricultural yield

USL's 'Accelerate to a Low-Carbon World' priority commits the Company to decarbonising operations, engaging its supply chain and strengthening business resilience in a low-carbon economy.

Relevance to United Spirits Limited
USL's manufacturing depends on climate-sensitive agricultural commodities — principally broken rice, grains and water 
— sourced predominantly from smallholder farmers in India. Supply chain disruptions caused by climate change, land degradation or unsustainable farming practices pose direct risks to raw material security and cost. Embedding regenerative agriculture and responsible sourcing into the supply base is therefore both a resilience imperative and a value-chain sustainability commitment.Relevance to United Spirits Limited
Product safety is the most fundamental obligation USL has to its consumers. In the Indian alcobev market characterised by complex excise structures, multi-state distribution and counterfeit risk — ensuring the consistent safety, quality and traceability of every product is a non-negotiable pillar of consumer trust and regulatory compliance. The Executive Committee elevated Product Safety to a standalone material topic in FY 2025–26, recognising its direct bearing on brand equity, consumer confidence and long-term enterprise value.

Relevance to United Spirits Limited
Strong corporate governance and ethical conduct are prerequisites for maintaining stakeholder confidence, regulatory 
goodwill and long-term enterprise value. For USL, operating in a complex regulatory environment with multiple excise and licensing authorities, a zero-tolerance approach to corruption, bribery and anti-competitive conduct is both a legal necessity and a cultural commitment. The Company's 'Doing Business the Right Way' philosophy underpins every aspect of governance — from Board accountability to frontline compliance training.Relevance to United Spirits Limited
The production and packaging of alcoholic beverages generates solid waste, packaging materials and liquid effluent across the product lifecycle. Irresponsible waste management creates environmental risks — including greenhouse gas emissions, soil and water pollution, and biodiversity loss — and carries regulatory and reputational consequences. USL is committed to a circular economy approach, targeting zero waste to landfill and sustainable packaging solutions across its operations.

The alcobev industry continues to grow as purchasing power, 
aspirations and normalisation of the category continue to evolve the category. With India at an inflexion point in its trajectory, being one of the fastest growing large economies of the world, driven by a consumption, anchored on a young population, the category remains vibrant and dynamic, with the narrative moving towards more nuanced play of aspiration, value, and responsibility.Operating Context
in a New IndiaShaping Growth India, the Consumer Market of the Decade
Fastest-growing large economy, with a median age of 28,  
a booming middle & high-income class, and a projected 
GDP of $7 trillion by 2030, India is reshaping global consumption trends.
A vibrant democracy with a digital-first economy, 
the future is being built here
We’re seeing a deeper, sharper INDIA CONFIDENCE, 
that’s driving how people spend, consumer and aspire
India now contributes 39% of growth in global  
Total Beverage Alcohol (TBA) and is the fastest growing large market in this space
India is the #1 whiskey market by volume, #2 by value, 
and the #3 spirits market globally. With per capita consumption at 2.6 litres, and spirits penetration significantly lower than average consumer goods categories, the runway for growth is massive
However, India is not one but many, and segmenting the country into relevant segments is critical. And being able to speak with a diverse portfolio catering to these different segments and needs is critical. One size does not fit all.The India story isn’t just about 
scale, it’s about quality of growth.

Premiumisation is being  
the New Normal
Consumption is steadily moving up the value chain, driven by 
aspiration, exposure and a growing preference for authenticity. Products today are evaluated basis taste, and story, and experience. This is gradually repositioning growth from volume expansion to value creation.
A New  Generation of Consumers 
is Reshaping Demand
Younger cohorts are entering the category with different expectations. Their choices reflect identity, experimentation and occasion which is also reflected in the rapidly expanding repertoire of brands that consumers engage with. Consumption is becoming more curated and intentional, where consumers choose different drinks for different occasions, deciding on preference of tastes, flavours, formats. Defining the Market Megatrends
This is driving growth through consumption of new drinks and experiences, and contrary to popular belief, is driving ‘drink better’ and not a reduction in consumption. therefore, influencing the portfolio development and brand relevance. 
“Experiences and Repertoires  
are Expanding”
New formats, flavour-led innovation and craft offerings are creating fresh occasions, while on-trade and curated spaces continue to shape perception and drive premium adoption. Convenience and experience are converging, opening new pathways for category expansion and increasingly consumers are increasing their repertoire, choosing different drinks for different occasions.39 Operating Context     CORPORATE OVERVIEW

How we are Reacting to these Megatrends
Our response is to move closer to where value is shifting. Our portfolio plays to the different segments in India, with an offering 
for each of the Indias for their different affordability/price points as well as their different occasions, by leveraging the trends of premiumisation, repertoire, experiences and LDA choices.
The portfolio now leans into premium and above, where choice is more considered. The growing presence of Bottled-in-
Origin scotch and tequila, and the rise of brands like Don Julio, reflect this shift. At the same time, we are strengthening our India play through The Good Craft Co. and investments in craft brands that carry a sense of place. Innovation stays close to evolving preferences, seen in flavours such as Minty Jamun and Mango Mirchi of Smirnoff, and in formats like the 180 ml packs that open new occasions.
Definition of engagement and operations are also getting a revamp. Digital platforms and cultural associations, across music, 
sports, fashion and lifestyle, enabling us to stay connected with consumers. Sustainability is becoming part of everyday decisions, from conservation-led storytelling through Godawan to our Grain-to-Glass approach. The regulatory environment remains fluid, and our focus is to stay responsive, adjusting quickly while maintaining discipline. The direction is clear, stay relevant, stay agile, and grow with intent.

Driving Profitable Growth in a Dynamic 
Environment
During the year, reported P&A growth remained resilient 
despite policy-led headwind in Maharashtra excluding the prior year pipeline fill impact in Andhra Pradesh, underlying performance reflects healthy structural momentum. Excluding Maharashtra, P&A volumes grew in mid-single digits, while NSV growth strengthened further, supported by continued premium mix expansion.
Price & mix improved significantly during the year, reflecting:
• Increased salience of the luxury and Bottled-in-Origin & 
Bottled in India portfolio.
• Sustained high single-digit to near to double-digit growth in Upper Prestige brands.
• Continued momentum in Indian single malt led by the CSD & the Indian Armed Forces Channel.
• Flavour-led innovation in Smirnoff including Minty Jamun, supported incremental growth and strengthened India’s position amongst Diageo’s key Smirnoff markets.
• Format innovation through Pocket Packs supported accessibility, penetration and mix improvement while reinforcing convenience-led consumption trends.
The Prestige and Above portfolio continued to anchor value creation, strengthening pricing power and operating leverage.
Premiumisation Powering Value Creation
We remain committed to navigating an evolving competitive and regulatory landscape by staying focused on portfolio and disciplined execution. The net sales salience of the Prestige & Above segment strengthened further, reflecting sustained consumer preference for high-quality & differentiated offerings.
Luxury brands expanded their cultural footprint and on-trade 
presence, supporting trial and long-term brand equity. Initiatives Undertaken During FY 2025-26 
Indian single malt Godawan and tequila Don Julio continued to scale rapidly, reinforcing leadership positions in emerging high-value categories. Smirnoff’s flavour innovation and Royal Challenge pocket packs expanded penetration and favourable mix development.
The structural shift towards premium offerings supports both 
topline growth and margin expansion. We remain committed to investing in the most effective levers of growth to create long-term value for all stakeholders.
Margin Expansion through Productivity 
and Pricing Discipline
Gross margin expanded during the year, supported by:
• Improved portfolio mix
• Calibrated pricing actions
• Strong cost productivity delivery
• Supply chain agility initiatives
On the cost side, the overall input basket remained 
manageable during the year. Bulk scotch continued to be structurally inflationary, underscoring the importance of mix-led growth, productivity and supply agility with potential medium-term relief expected upon implementation of the India-U.K. Free Trade Agreement. Our multi-year supply agility programme continued to optimise manufacturing footprint, logistics efficiency, and inventory management.
Marketing reinvestment remained disciplined and consistent 
with long-term brand building priorities. Advertising & Promotion (A&P) remained within the guided range, balancing growth investment with profitability discipline.
EBITDA growth outpaced revenue growth, reflecting operating 
leverage, favourable portfolio mix and cost optimisation.Healthy Performance Across Financial Metrics

Continued focus on productivity and operational efficiencies supported 11.6% EBITDA growth and an EBITDA Margin of 18.4%.

Environment Health and Safety
Our operations are underpinned by a Zero Harm philosophy, extending to the environment and every individual who works with us. 
Safety is embedded into how assets are designed, maintained, and operated, guided by a six-pillar strategy spanning Governance, Risk Mitigation & Management, Safety Culture, Digitisation & Analytics, Environment, and ERC (Engagement, Recognition & Certifications). 
We maintain high standards of hygiene and quality across 
our owned and third-party manufacturing facilities to meet customer safety expectations and evolving consumer aspirations. Our operations comply with the regulations of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), State Excise authorities, and the Legal Metrology Rules (LMR), supported by robust internal controls, quality standards, and assurance practices.
Our quality management approach spans  the entire value 
chain – from product design and raw material sourcing 
to finished product delivery – ensuring trust in every drop. All finished products undergo stringent quality checks supported by a positive release system. Under the Global Product Integrity Testing Programme 100% Compliance (GPIP), products are tested to ensure they are free from contaminants and safe for consumers. Our sensory panel members are qualified through rigorous training and validations including external agency validations such as Neutral Spirits Sensory Proficiency Scheme (NSSPS).
We maintain strong internal laboratory standards across 
all manufacturing units to ensure product quality and compliance. Our laboratories are regularly validated through external assessments, including the Diageo Alcohol Proficiency Scheme compliance (DAPS), reinforcing the reliability and integrity of our quality assurance systems.Global Risk Management 
System (GRMS) adhered to across all business units, with audits, safety walkabouts, and visible felt leadership.Programmes such as i-Drive Safe, SBO, PSM (Process Safety Management), and campaigns like National Safety Week and Road Safety Week build ownership at every level.Digital LOTO, Permit to Work, MOC (Management of Change), and upcoming modules for BBS, CAPA, EHS Audit, HIRA & HAZOP strengthen intelligent safety management.

Grain-to-glass Food Safety Quality Framework 
We ensure stringent quality standards across every stage of the value chain through a comprehensive risk assessment framework. 
Our quality norms and inspection processes are continuously strengthened by integrating best-in-class practices, digital technologies, Global Risk Management Standards (GRMS), local regulatory requirements, and automation into our systems and processes.

Our FSSAI-certified units adhere to stringent quality controls across all processes, including material inspection, 
in-process quality monitoring, final product evaluation, and pre-dispatch checks. All manufacturing facilities are certified 
under globally recognised standards such as FSSC 22000 for food safety and ISO 9001 for quality management.
In line with our ‘One Manufacturing’ approach, we actively collaborate with third-party manufacturers to enhance 
technology adoption, build capabilities, and strengthen systems, processes, and infrastructure.
We engage external partners to assess finished goods quality in line with Diageo’s Global Distribution Quality 
Standards. This includes annual on-shelf quality reviews, competitor benchmarking, and quarterly market 
connect reviews with internal quality teams. Insights from these assessments are leveraged to drive continuous, 
consumer-focused quality improvements.
We have a robust consumer concerns management system with a fast turnaround time and a tiered governance 
mechanism extending to senior leadership, ensuring prompt resolution of consumer issues. Root Cause Problem 
Solving (RCPS) is implemented, with learnings deployed across manufacturing sites where applicable.
We have also introduced Consumer Satisfaction (CSAT) surveys to enhance consumer experience. Additionally, 
our automated smart flow management system ensures all consumer queries are effectively tracked and resolved

A Culture of Food Safety and Quality Excellence
We have embedded a strong food safety and quality culture across all levels of the organisation to ensure consistent product integrity and enhance 
customer and consumer satisfaction. Our approach is anchored in three key pillars:
Rigorous Standards and Process 
Excellence
We mitigate quality risks and safeguard consumers 
through processes aligned with Global Risk Management Standards (GRMS) and FSSAI regulations, including a structured product recall mechanism. Oversight is provided by central and site-level steering committees, supported by a Crisis Management Team (CMT) chaired by the MD and CEO. Annual mock recalls are conducted to strengthen emergency preparedness.
All products undergo stringent quality checks, including 
hourly inspections across packaging lines supported by a positive release mechanism. We also monitor distribution quality at the first point of sale to assess product integrity during transit and drive improvements. Additionally, annual third-party on-shelf assessments are conducted based on Consumer Relevant Quality Standards (CRQS), along with competitor benchmarking. These insights and quality KPIs are continuously tracked to ensure consistent product delivery and reinforce consumer confidence.
Cross-functional Collaboration
We conduct regular cross-functional review forums to enable early risk identification, facilitate knowledge sharing, and ensure alignment on quality goals across the organisation.Building Quality Capabilities 
Organisation-wide
We have a qualified and capable team of food safety 
and quality professionals overseeing quality control and assurance across the value chain. New joiners undergo comprehensive induction and refresher training, including sensory and on-the-job training modules.
Capability-building initiatives include weekly ‘Gurukul’ 
training sessions covering quality standards, global practices, and internal SOPs for manufacturing teams, as well as the ‘RISE Together’ programme for cross-functional learning at supplier locations. We also participate in external certifications, awards, and platforms such as CII, ICQC, and RBNQA to gain an external perspective and drive continuous improvement.
We have established Centres of Excellence in liquid and 
packaging quality, supported by specialised external training and certification programmes.Scaling Manufacturing Competitiveness
Supply Chain and Distribution 
Excellence 
We have a robust end-to-end supply chain network, 
comprising 2,400+ sourcing suppliers and a distribution network of 10 primary depots, and 2,000+ primary distributors. This network ensures ready raw material availability for seamless production while maintaining operational agility.
We undertake comprehensive efforts towards 
strengthening supply chain resilience. These include: 
•
 Supplier selection based on their ability to deliver 
ser

manner.

 Structured evaluations and mont

 Recognising high-performing suppliers thr
ough the

 Know Your Business Partner (KYBP) standard ensure
s all

In FY 2025-26, we continued with our Supply Chain Agility Programme towards making our network leaner and more efficient. Key developments include: 
Footprint optimisation 
Under our supply chain agility programme, manufacturing facilities have been rationalised to 36 units using the FSD (Factory-SKU-Depot) linear programming model, targeting one scaled facility per state to minimise interstate movement and associated costs. 
Co-locating 
All bottling plants are co-located with Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA) distillation units to streamline production and reduce transportation costs.

Brand Heritage
McDowell’s is one of India’s most iconic and most 
loved whisky brand. Established in 1898 and having a legacy spanning over a century, the brand has evolved alongside the Indian consumer, building a strong nationwide presence across generations. Over the decades, McDowell’s has successfully combined consistency in quality with sharp cultural relevance, enabling it to remain one of the most recognised and trusted names in the industry. 
At the heart of McDowell’s lies the enduring philosophy

Godawan
Sustainable, Mindful 
Indian Luxury
Godawan is an artisanal single-malt whisky crafted in 
Rajasthan using locally sourced six-row barley and matured in the state’s warm, dry climate with temperatures reaching 100ºF at The Godawan Distillery, Rajasthan. It is a tribute to the land’s heritage and the majestic Great Indian Bustard (GIB), a native endangered species named Godawan. 
The liquid was originally launched in two expressions, 
Godawan 01 Rich and Rounded, and Godawan 02 Fruit and Spice. The brand continues to introduce distinctive new expressions to scale Indian single malt on the global stage, while promoting awareness and conservation of GIB. A portion of the proceeds from the sale of every bottle goes into the Godawan bird conservation.Godawan 01 and 02
Crafted for global travellers 
This latest expression is crafted at the Alwar distillery in Rajasthan, inspired by the region’s intricate jaali woodwork, a symbol of finesse and artistry.
The whisky introduces a new dimension of flavour and depth while staying rooted in the 
brand’s mindful luxury and provenance. It is matured in ex-bourbon casks and finished in a rare combination of PX sherry, virgin oak, and cherry wood casks. It is a golden-brown liquid with 46% ABV, with floral and fruity aromas, a sweet, textured palate and a light, balanced wood finish. 
It is exclusively created for global travel retail, with airport duty-free as the primary 
channel, given their growing significance as high-impact brand discovery zones for consumers, where gifting, collecting, and connection converge. The whisky is presently available in Dubai, Bengaluru, Mumbai, and Delhi Duty Free Stores.Godawan Triple Cask 
Travel Exclusive98

Slow Batch DistilledThe Singleton

When the world was deep into its gin revival, India still had little it could call its own. NAO Spirits spotted that gap early. 
What began in a small Goan distillery soon became one of the clearest signals in Indian alcobev. Through brands such as Greater Than and Hapusa, NAO created craft spirits that felt rooted in Indian botanicals, local provenance and a fresh cultural point of view. Diageo India recognised in NAO an early mover that had shaped the category with originality and credibility. Diageo India completed the acquisition of NAO Spirits during FY 2025-26. Bringing the brands into its fold marks a strategic step towards scaling a homegrown craft story that is closely aligned with the evolving Indian palate.
Greater Than brought a new kind of craft story to the market. Distilled using 9 botanicals sourced from India and around the world, it combines strong quality credentials with broad cocktail versatility. Recognised by the Gin Guild, it remains the only London Dry Gin from South Asia to receive this distinction. Crisp in character and contemporary in design, it is built for everything from a classic Gin and Tonic (G&T) to a well-made cocktail, with minimalist packaging that stands out effortlessly on shelves across markets.

Hapusa is rooted entirely in India’s botanical landscape. It is 
distilled with Himalayan juniper and layered with coriander seeds, turmeric, ginger, gondhoraj, cardamom, mango and almond sourced from across the country. The result is a gin with a sense of place, depth and distinction. Hapusa has quietly become a favourite with seasoned Gin

Distilled in Goa from local jaggery, it is matured for two years in Port Wine casks imported from Portugal. A finishing touch of jaggery and three spices black pepper, cinnamon and clove add warmth, character and a subtle nod to the flavours that once drew Portuguese explorers to India’s western coast. Rich in story and layered in taste, PIPA offers an Indian origin story with a spirit shaped by cultural exchange.
PIPA has been slowly making its presence felt across Goa, Italy and UK. It is now

Packaging Innovation
We are advancing packaging innovation to deliver on our 
sustainability commitments. This ensures our formats to be recyclable, reusable, or compostable. Increasingly lighter glass bottles that can survive multiple washing and service cycles with higher cullet or recycled content have also been part of our key focus areas.
In parallel, we are upgrading our packaging to meet dynamic 
consumer expectations through blending functionality, aesthetics, and convenience. This includes creating premium designs and the material being lighter, efficient, and environmentally responsible. Packaging innovation accelerates our sustainability agenda and strengthens brand equity. It also responds to the needs of a more conscious and discerning consumer. Aligned with our ‘Spirit of Progress - Society 2030’ ambition & India PWM legislation, we drive compliant initiatives such as shifts from glass to PET, lightweighting and improved circularity. These solutions reduce environmental impact, reduce cost efficiency, and enhance consumer experience.
Reimagining Packaging for 
Scale and Sustainability
We are transitioning from energy-intensive glass to 
low-carbon PET and rPET formats, while progressing lightweighting initiatives and digital traceability solutions. These efforts strengthen environmental performance, improve product integrity, and enable stronger consumer interface and trust.

The Good Craft Co. Ethos and Philosophy
The Good Craft Co. brings these stories to 
life, celebrating the makers, ingredients, and traditions defining Indian craftsmanship. From sourcing and provenance to indigenous distillation, maturation, and artisanal finishing, the platform highlights the depth and diversity of Indian craft traditions.
Established in 2022 at our Ponda distillery in 
Goa, The Good Craft Co. brings together craft makers, startups, enthusiasts, and industry experts to nurture innovation and strengthen the craft spirits ecosystem. Designed as a direct-to-consumer experiential initiative, it offers immersive experiences that introduce consumers to the processes, ingredients, and heritage that define Indian craft spirits.A platform built on six pillars of doing good to nurture exceptional Indian craft spirits and a thriving ecosystem of start-ups across the Indian spirits industry.
India’s craft spirits 
carry a legacy of ingredients, 
craftsmanship, and 
provenance that is only beginning to be discovered.
We, along with our venture arms, are actively seeking partnerships with early and 
growth-stage companies that can disrupt the Indian beverage alcohol space with new products, formats, or capabilities. Our investments in emerging homegrown brands such as NAO Spirits, Pistola, Quaffine, and Sober, reflect a strategic focus on shaping future consumption trends in India. We are strengthening our presence in premium and craft spirits categories by backing NAO Spirits – the largest Indian gin brand and Pistola in the fast-growing agave segment (growing ~100% Y-o-Y).
Investments in Quaffine tap into the rising demand for mid proof drinks, with the category expected to grow 60-70% over the next five years, while Sober enables Diageo to participate in the large and evolving non-drinking population of ~830 million consumers.
These investments allow us to diversify the portfolio, capture high-growth white 
spaces, and stay ahead of shifting consumer preferences through locally relevant, innovative brands. Doing Good

Extending Safety 
Across the Value ChainGovernance, Safety Assessments 
and Audits
EHS performance is strengthened through a multi-level 
governance and assurance framework that drives accountability and sustained focus on critical risks. All units follow a defined schedule of self assessments against Global Risk Management Standards, with findings translated into time-bound action plans tracked through closure.
Site Heads review performance monthly through Manufacturing 
Operations Reviews and Management Review Meetings, helping remove barriers, reinforce standards, and sustain momentum on corrective actions.
The governance framework is supported by internal and 
external audits across key themes, including SFIP audits, ISO audits, and risk-based assessments such as electrical audits, in plant traffic assessments, thermography, and fire risk surveys. During the year, focused EHS audits led jointly by Regional EHS Leads and EHS Managers further strengthened audit quality and enabled wider sharing of best practices across sites.Focus on Safety Culture and 
Visible Felt Leadership
Aligned with our Zero Harm aspiration, we continue to 
strengthen a safety-first culture across the workplace, on the road, and beyond the workplace. Our approach focuses on building consistent safe behaviours and deepening personal ownership, so that safety remains integral to everyday decision-making at every level of the organisation.
Line managers play a central role through visible felt 
leadership, supported by regular safety walkabouts and structured safe behaviour observations. These interventions help identify unsafe conditions, recognise safe practices, and enable timely correction and coaching. Our Behaviour-Based Safety approach further strengthens discipline by translating observations into actionable learnings that can be applied consistently across sites.

Hazard Identification, Risk Assessment, Training 
and Incident Investigation
Safety performance is monitored through a balanced focus 
on leading and lagging indicators, supported by structured reporting through Safety Improvement Report Cards accessible to all employees. Employees are encouraged to report hazards, unsafe conditions, and near misses, enabling potential incidents to be identified early and addressed proactively.
Formal hazard identification and risk assessment processes 
are carried out across activities, with gaps addressed through corrective actions and residual risks reviewed after controls are implemented. Regular training strengthens capabilities to identify risks, investigate incidents, and apply learnings consistently in day-to-day operations. Incident learnings are shared across the organisation to strengthen preventive measures and support broader deployment of effective controls.
Safety Communication, Engagement and 
Continual Improvement
Governance: EHS performance is sustained through 
disciplined governance, clear communication, and workforce engagement. Daily Tier 1 shopfloor reviews under the SQDCMS framework ensure safety remains a priority and enable immediate escalation of concerns. Performance is further reviewed at Department Head and Unit Management levels. Each unit operates a Central Safety Committee, with equal representation from workers and management and chaired by the Unit Head, to review KPIs, resolve issues, and track actions to closure.
Communication: Clear and consistent communication 
reinforces EHS priorities across the organisation. This includes monthly safety campaigns focused on SFIP standards, town halls, and targeted as well as organisation-wide training programmes. 
Continual improvement: Continual improvement is driven 
through Kaizen, One Page Learning, Safety Action Meetings, and Focused Improvement projects using the DMAIC framework, alongside Yellow and Green Belt initiatives. Safety Improvement Report Cards further support structured identification, prioritisation, and closure of unsafe conditions.
Health and Safety Initiatives 
During the year, the Company strengthened its safety agenda by focusing on high risk areas and advancing system-led improvements that embed prevention into daily operations. The overall effort centred on stronger process discipline, wider digital adoption, and sharper risk visibility across sites. This approach improved assurance, standardised critical workflows, and supported timely closure of actions while reinforcing safety as a consistent operating priority.Digitisation
Digitisation of core safety processes strengthened compliance, traceability, and response effectiveness. This includes digitisation of the Work Permit System under Control of Work, the Safety Management System covering safety observations, automated CAPA and audit management, and Management of Change. The Company has already deployed Digitised Work Permit System, Management of Changed (MOC) and now have initiated deployment of an EHS Portal as a single system of record, with a phased eight module rollout planned over approximately 16 months covering Behaviour-Based Safety, EHS Audits, Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA), Hazard and Operability Study (HAZOP), and Aspect–Impact management.
Road safety governance for business driving was strengthened 
through deployment of the Autobeacon mobile application, which uses smartphone-based indicators such as over speeding, harsh braking, rapid acceleration, and distracted driving to generate trip-level Safe Driving Scores and enable timely coaching and corrective actions.

Advancing Process Safety Management
During the year, process safety was strengthened through 
release of the PSM Policy under Chief Supply Officer sponsorship, enhanced leading and lagging indicators, and development of internal HAZOP capabilities. Process Safety Information, including P&IDs and supporting documentation, was upgraded to ensure decisions are based on current and reliable risk information.
Governance reviews supported by area-wise PSM scorecards 
strengthened oversight, accountability, and follow through on critical controls. All new projects and process modifications undergo MOC process and through studies – HAZOP and Quantitative Risk Assessment (QRA), with safeguards incorporated early in design to strengthen safe start-up and reduce risk prior to commissioning.Strengthening Safety Management Systems
ISO 45001, ISO 14001, and ISO 9001 certifications were achieved across own manufacturing units, reinforcing a structured and auditable approach to occupational health, environmental management, and quality systems. These expectations are being extended across the value chain through engagement with third-party manufacturers. Eight partner units are certified to ISO 45001, and ISO 14001 certification processes have been initiated for identified partners.
Focused Safety Interventions
A phased upgrade of forklifts to defined Gold Standards was initiated across own manufacturing units to reduce material handling and vehicle interaction risks. The programme includes advanced safety devices, standardised operating practices, and stronger controls to improve operating discipline and reduce collision risk.
The “Safe Day in Trade” campaign was launched to address 
safety risks faced by commercial and sales teams during market visits, building awareness and promoting consistent safe practices in the field.
Leadership, Communication and Engagement
Visible felt leadership and proactive communication remain central to sustaining a zero harm culture. Safety is reinforced through leadership tone, safety as the first agenda item in key forums, executive safety walkabouts and Behaviour-Based Safety observations, monthly EHS campaigns aligned to key risks, structured training calendars, cross-functional improvement teams, and enterprise-wide observances such as National Safety Month, National Road Safety Month, International Safety Week, Environment Day, and Fire Safety Week.Recognition

Preserve Water for Life
Water stewardship has been a longstanding priority for us, and we are focused on preserving this critical resource, particularly in water-stressed areas. Water is the most important ingredient in our products, and it’s been a longstanding priority for us. It is also a precious shared resource that is facing increasing pressure in many parts of the world caused by the impacts of climate change and the competing demands for freshwater resources. Since our inception in India, we have made notable advancements in water efficiency and sustainability. Our initiatives include the adoption of innovative technologies within our facilities and active participation in community projects, such as reforestation, wetland restoration, pond desilting, water capture and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) programmes. 
Water Replenishment
We recognise the need for collaboration, and partner with multiple stakeholders to create solutions that improve water security. Since 2015, we have implemented several community water programmes. Our goal is to contribute to a net positive impact on catchment water resources, particularly in priority basins and water-stressed areas.
Our strategic actions for water in our 
communities include:
Replenish more water than we use at our sites in 
water-stressed areas
Since FY 2016-17, we have implemented various water 
replenishment projects around our owned operations  to create water replenishment capacity of more than 1.6 million CuM through an inclusive, multistakeholder approach. Various projects including desilting of ponds, construction of rainwater harvesting structures, building check dams etc. have been implemented in states including Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Odisha. We continue to work on providing access to clean  drinking water and sanitation facilities to our communities. In FY 2025-26, we expanded our work in the states of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.

The Godavari Initiative (TGI) has been envisioned as a 
multi-stakeholder collaborative for promoting equitable management & source sustainability of the Godavari River Basin in Maharashtra through benefit-sharing, stakeholder engagement, and practical learning. TGI aims to create a multi-stakeholder collaborative platform for corporates, government, and civil society to address critical challenges related to river basin health and climate resilience, through collective action. Being the founding member of TGI, we are working in partnership with various Govt. departments focusing on the Godavari River catchment-based solutions. In FY 2025-26, we have entered an Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Nashik Municipal Corporation (NMC) to work on restoring the river health through multiple waste management initiatives. Suppliers 
with our ESG 
AspirationsWe follow a structured process to onboard suppliers. This includes 
evaluating risk profile (based on country risks, supplier spends and key input materials), operational and strategic importance, and their alignment with our ‘Spirit of Progress’ and the Responsible Sourcing framework. The process encompasses standardised selection templates and sustainability questionnaires on parameters like labour standards, human rights (including child and forced labour), environmental performance and legal compliance. These elements are integrated into all contracts and bidding processes, with contractual obligations for all suppliers.
For all high-risk supplier partners enhanced due diligence is 
mandated. High Risk Suppliers are evaluated basis country risks, supplier spends and key input materials. They must register with SEDEX and complete its Self-Assessment Questionnaire (SAQ), aligned with our Responsible Sourcing programme. High-risk suppliers are also required to undergo independent audits as per the SMETA four-pillar audit protocol or its equivalent. This is monitored and reviewed monthly and necessary actions are taken on need basis.
We believe that early awareness of potential breaches enables 
us to respond swiftly and effectively. Every report is treated with the utmost seriousness, and we firmly uphold a zero-tolerance policy against any retaliation from a Diageo employee towards suppliers or agency partners who raise concerns in good faith or assist with investigations. We encourage our suppliers and agency partners to share any issues regarding our business practices, or possible violations of our Standard or Code of Business Conduct, directly with their Diageo contact. Alternatively, concerns may be submitted through our SpeakUp service – a confidential platform available to employees and third parties (including suppliers), operated independently by an external company. SpeakUp offers trained staff who can support callers in their local languages, and is accessible via telephone, email, or internet, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.168 169 Social and Relationship Capital – Responsible Supply Chain     CORPORATE OVERVIEW

Country Risk and Key input materials)are audited on SMETA 4-Pillar and identified gaps are being addressed through structured engagement and corrective action plans.We want to make a positive contribution to human 
rights and society. We are committed to promoting and respecting human rights throughout our supply chain and expect the same from our suppliers and agency partners. 
We are committed to acting in accordance with the UN 
Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights and the international standards set out by the eight core International Labour Organisation (ILO) conventions and recommendations. We expect our suppliers and agency partners to act in accordance with these principles and commitments, and we have minimum standards in the following areas:
Prevention of Child Labour 
We expect our suppliers and agency partners to adhere to applicable laws and regulations concerning minimum working age, and strictly to prohibit the employment of young persons below the age of 15 (subject to exceptions permitted by national law or the ILO); and to protect and promote the special interests of employees under 18 by allowing them access to education, limiting employment during typical resting hours, and ensuring no exposure to working conditions that are likely to jeopardise their health and safety or morals. 
Children and young workers are key to the Sedex 
Members Ethical Trade Audit (SMETA) methodology and age verification takes place through the review of documents including policies and procedures in place to manage child labour. Another key method to prevent child labour through the audit is the focus put on ensuring hiring practices are including thorough checks on the ages of applicants and how this can be verified.

Defining the Customer Cohorts
India is not a single consumer story, but a market defined by three distinct cohorts. As the three cohorts continue to 
expand; they reflect the broader rise of affluence and aspiration across the country. Our portfolio is structured around these cohorts, with a clear role in driving premiumisation across each.
Primarily part of the 
service economy and include Uber drivers, entry level professionals, service providers, retail workers, sales/ops/factory workers, gig economy and entry-level professionalsProverbial middle class and the backbone of India’s consumption economy spanning salaried mid-level professionals, government employees, the self-employed, legacy businessmen, and new entrepreneurs.Traditionally wealthy and a rising set of young entrepreneurs with new wealth. This cohort comprises higher-income salaried professionals and owners of scaled businesses.

Accelerate to a Low-carbon World
Our Carbon Strategy
Our commitment to decarbonising operations and the value chain is anchored in a science-based, technology-led 
approach. Focus remains on activating key decarbonisation levers and strengthening collaboration to mitigate climate risks, build resilience and enable a sustained transition towards a low-carbon economy.
Net Zero  
Roadmap 2050
Our commitment to decarbonisation is aligned with 
global climate goals. We target Net Zero across direct operations by 2040 and across the value chain by 2050, in line with Diageo plc and the Paris Agreement. Progress is anchored in a science-based pathway, measured against a 2022 baseline* to ensure transparency and accountability.
This pathway continues to evolve with the business. 
In 2025, the Science Based Targets initiative approved updated targets, reflecting learnings from the initial phase of the ‘Spirit of Progress’ journey. Revised baselines and a clearer classification of emissions into Forest, Land, and Agriculture (FLAG) and non-FLAG categories strengthen the precision and relevance of our decarbonisation approach.Mitigation

Protecting the Godawan
In Rajasthan, we support Project W (GIB) with implementation partner 
Gramodaya Samajik Sansthan (GSS), focused on the in-situ conservation of the Great Indian Bustard (Godawan), one of the country's most critically endangered species. Key initiatives include restoring water bodies, developing nesting habitats, and building community awareness in the arid grasslands of Rajasthan.
Afforestation and Ecosystem Restoration
We continued to expand our green footprint through sustained afforestation efforts, building on plantations established in previous years while adding new sites during FY 2025-26. Focus remained on improving survival rates, enhancing biodiversity value, and strengthening carbon sequestration potential. Ensuring  Responsible Business Conduct
Code of Conduct
At Diageo India, the Code of Business Conduct guides employees in upholding ethical behaviour, integrity, 
and organisational values. It aligns with the global policies of the principal shareholder, Diageo plc, and sets out standards and guidelines across key areas of work. All employees complete a mandatory annual e-learning module as part of the Company’s compliance certification programme. New joiners are required to complete this training within 30 days of joining.
Anti-Corruption and Anti-Bribery
Diageo India maintains a zero-tolerance approach to corruption and bribery. The Company follows a comprehensive global anti-corruption policy established by its principal shareholder, Diageo plc, which addresses all forms of bribery and corruption. The core elements of this policy are embedded within the Code of Business Conduct and apply across all operations, including subsidiaries and value chain partners.
Whistle-blower Mechanism
Employees and value chain partners are encouraged to report any actual or suspected breaches of the Code of Conduct or Company policies through the confidential ‘Speak Up’ channel, managed by an independent external party. This channel is accessible via telephone, email, website, and QR code. Employees may also raise concerns through internal channels, including Business Integrity members, and the Human Resources and Legal departments, with assurance of protection from retaliation.
Respect for human rights remains integral to how we operate. Our approach is guided by Diageo plc’s Global Human Rights Policy, aligned with internationally recognised human rights charters. This policy reinforces our commitment to protecting and promoting the rights of all stakeholders, including employees, supply chain workers and partners, consumers, and communities where we operate. Our Dignity at Work policy, aligned with local laws and cultural norms, defines clear standards for personal integrity and conduct. These expectations extend to our suppliers through the Partnering with Suppliers Standard.
An annual legal compliance risk assessment is conducted under 
the supervision of the Risk Management Committee, covering areas such as human rights, bribery, and corruption. Human rights remain a key focus within the SEDEX Members Ethical Trade Audit (SMETA) four-pillar audits for high-risk suppliers, in line with Supplier Ethical Data Exchange (Sedex) protocols, as part of our responsible sourcing programme. Our Human Rights Impact Assessments (HRIAs) identify salient risks and vulnerable stakeholders across both our operations and supply chain.Institutionalising Integrity and
